acceptance_criteria.criterion: Calling StartAsync while a run is in progress throws InvalidOperationException synchronously before scheduling any work.
Cancel signals the token; the scanner stops between files; state returns to Idle after the run completes.
StateChanged fires for every transition: Idle → Running, then Running → Completed (or Faulted).
CancellationTokenSource is always disposed on run completion, including on fault.
Two concurrent StartAsync calls cannot both enter the running state (no TOCTOU gap from Interlocked.CompareExchange).

summary: Created RefreshStateChangedEventArgs (VideoIndexer.Core/Events/) following the established ShellStateChangedEventArgs pattern.

Updated IRefreshOrchestrator: added StateChanged event (was specified in WP-002 description but omitted from the delivered file), and updated StartRefreshAsync doc to correctly describe the InvalidOperationException on concurrent calls.

Implemented RefreshOrchestrator.cs: single-flight guard via Interlocked.CompareExchange on a dedicated _runningFlag int; state machine (Idle→Running→Completed/Faulted/Idle) tracked via Volatile.Read/Write on _stateValue int; CTS always disposed in finally; CancelRefresh via volatile _cts field.
Cancellation path sets state back to Idle (cts.IsCancellationRequested check); fault path sets state to Faulted; normal completion sets state to Completed.
Task.Run uses CancellationToken.None so cancellation of the scan is handled inside RefreshAsync, preventing CTS disposal race on early Task cancellation.
All 262 existing tests pass; build is clean with 0 warnings.

comments.note: IRefreshOrchestrator.cs (WP-002 deliverable) was missing the StateChanged event and had incorrect doc for StartRefreshAsync (described no-op semantics instead of the specified throw). Fixed as part of this WP since nothing consumed the interface yet. The WP-002 QA/review pipelines did not catch this omission.

RefreshOrchestrator uses a separate _runningFlag int for the single-flight guard rather than encoding it in _stateValue. This keeps the CAS expression simple (compare against a single expected value: 0) while _stateValue freely tracks Idle/Completed/Faulted without needing special-casing. A future refactor could unify both into a single int if the state machine grows, but the current split is clear and correct.

The cancellation path sets state back to Idle (not a new Cancelled state) since RefreshState has no Cancelled variant. This is consistent with the enum design but means callers cannot distinguish a cancelled run from a clean restart when State == Idle. If a Cancelled state is added in a future milestone, the TransitionState call in the cancellation branch should be updated.

summary: Fixed two bugs in RefreshOrchestratorTests that caused a test failure and an indefinite hang.

Bug 1 (CancelRefresh_SignalsCancellationToken_AndStateReturnsToIdle): Scanner mock used Task.Delay(Timeout.Infinite, ct) which throws TaskCanceledException on cancel. The orchestrator catches all exceptions as faults, so state was Faulted instead of Idle. Fixed by replacing with a cooperative cancellation loop (while(!ct.IsCancellationRequested) await Task.Delay(5, CancellationToken.None)) that returns normally.

Bug 2 (AfterCancellation_NewRunCanBeStarted_ConfirmsFinally_Ran — the 6000s hang): The second StartRefreshAsync call used the same looping scanner but CancelRefresh() was never called, so the scanner looped forever. Fixed by calling CancelRefresh() immediately after the second start and awaiting the task directly instead of using NotThrowAsync().
All 14 RefreshOrchestrator tests pass (0 failures, 0 skipped). 3 killed stale testhost processes that were locking DLLs from the previous hung run.

comments.note: TaskCanceledException is a subclass of OperationCanceledException, which the orchestrator's catch block (catch Exception when ex is not OperationCanceledException) is designed to exclude. But the test's Task.Delay(Timeout.Infinite, ct) ran inside Task.Run with CancellationToken.None, so the thrown exception was not OperationCanceledException from the cancellation path — instead it was caught as a generic fault. The fix shifts responsibility for cancellation-awareness to the scanner mock (cooperative loop), matching the contract that RefreshAsync returns normally on cancellation.

The AfterCancellation test only verified the second run could start; it didn't assert State == Idle after the second run. The fix implicitly validates this by awaiting the second run's task after CancelRefresh, but an explicit State assertion could be added for clarity in a future pass.

comments.note: WaitForState test helper (RefreshOrchestratorTests.cs): Task.Delay(pollMs, timeout.Token) throws OperationCanceledException when the CancellationTokenSource fires, which propagates out of the while loop and bypasses the 'throw new TimeoutException(...)' line entirely. Fixed by wrapping the await Task.Delay call in a try/catch (OperationCanceledException) when (timeout.IsCancellationRequested) { break; } block so the helper now exits the loop cleanly and throws the intended TimeoutException with the diagnostic state message. All 14 tests pass post-fix.

[documentation-forward] ILibraryScanner.RefreshAsync (src/VideoIndexer.Core/Abstractions/ILibraryScanner.cs) must document the cooperative-cancellation contract that RefreshOrchestrator relies on: the scanner implementation MUST return normally when the cancellation token is signalled rather than throwing OperationCanceledException. RefreshOrchestrator's catch (Exception ex) block catches all exceptions — including OperationCanceledException — and treats them as faults (logs 'Library refresh faulted', sets state to Faulted). An implementor following the standard .NET cancellation pattern (throwing OCE) would produce spurious fault logs and leave the orchestrator in the Faulted state instead of Idle after a cancelled run. Add a '<remarks>' or '<exception>' note to RefreshAsync documenting this requirement.

[documentation-forward] RefreshOrchestrator.cs (src/VideoIndexer.Infrastructure/Library/RefreshOrchestrator.cs): The class-level <remarks> block describes the state machine and CTS disposal guarantee but does not cross-reference the cooperative-cancel contract required of ILibraryScanner. Once the ILibraryScanner doc is updated (see high-priority documentation-forward above), add a sentence in RefreshOrchestrator's remarks noting that the class depends on scanners returning normally on cancellation, and that any OperationCanceledException thrown by the scanner is treated as an unhandled fault by design.
